report.source_text: The patient was referred to the Department of Clinical Dermatology with initial treatment of 5 mg prednisone twice daily. After DIF results, a definitive diagnosis of PV was obtained, and 40 mg of systemic prednisone was prescribed along with nystatin antifungal (100000 per 3 mL) mouthwash. A week later, the dose was increased to 60 mg daily with continued use of nystatin mouthwash. After two weeks of the continued use of systemic prednisone, a significant improvement was seen, followed by a period of maintenance where the dose decreased gradually down to 5 mg daily (Figures 7, 8).

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 42-year-old Saudi male presented with diffuse ulceration in the oral cavity and skin lesions on the dorsal hand and nasal sill, along with dysphagia, dehydration, and weight loss. Initial empirical treatment with corticosteroids led to relapse. Physical examination revealed erythema multiforme-like skin lesions and desquamative gingivitis with diffuse oral erosions. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) on oral mucosal biopsy confirmed intercellular IgG and C3 deposition in a mesh-like pattern localized to basal and suprabasal layers, confirming Pemphigus Vulgaris. Subsequent systemic prednisone treatment resulted in significant clinical improvement.
